points: Yirmiyahu is a kohen, son of a kohen gadol, from Anasos in Binyamin. The Malbim: he didn't grow up in Yerushalayim, so people there might take him seriously.
He prophesies under three kings: Yoshiyahu (righteous), Yehoyakim and Tzidkiyahu, the last navi before the churban.
Like Moshe, he pushes back: "I can't speak, I'm only a boy." The Abarbanel finds 16 similarities between Yirmiyahu and Moshe, and says his young age shows in his simple language.
Two visions: an almond stick (punishment is coming fast) and a boiling pot from the north (Bavel). The Malbim: a pot with no cover; no fortress helps without Hashem's protection.
Hashem promises: they'll fight you but won't overcome you, I am with you. A navi, like a rabbi, makes comfortable people uncomfortable, and we all have that prophetic voice within us.
